consensus_expectations: Capital IQ consensus (data as of ~2026-08-05/08-10): FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA EUR951.85m (mean, 10-13 analysts) sits inside the upper half of management's EUR910-960m guided range, matching management's own upgraded steer -- guidance-consensus module verdict 'Bar is fair.' FY2026 revenue consensus EUR15,653.2m (+11.3% YoY, 14 analysts); FCF consensus EUR220.14m (~10% above the >EUR200m guided floor, though drifting down ~EUR22m since guidance was set). Revision activity on core operating lines has been flat/near-flat over 30-90 days -- a quiet, non-debating tape. BUT: Target Price consensus (mean EUR37.97) and Recommendation (Hold, 2.86) are explicitly flagged as deal-contaminated -- a cluster of large target-price/recommendation revisions from 2026-07-16 to 2026-07-24 re-anchored to Uber's announced acquisition approach rather than to a fresh fundamentals re-rate, so the operating-line consensus (fair bar) and the price-target consensus (deal-driven) are answering two different questions.
market_implied_expectations: Reverse-DCF (same WACC 7.45%, terminal g 3.0%, 7-yr horizon as the intrinsic DCF): at the current deal-contaminated price of EUR37.20, the market is pricing ~16.47% annual FCF growth for 7 straight years (or a steady-state Adjusted EBITDA margin of 7.48%, above the intrinsic-DCF module's own deliberately-capped 7.2% ceiling) -- assessed as 'aggressive' because it requires profit growth to reaccelerate against a two-year decelerating trend (+23.7%->+14.4%->+11.3% consensus) on a business with 'No moat proven' (group ROIC 0.8%-1.6% vs a company-disclosed 10.7%-13.7% cost of capital). At the pre-announcement price (EUR15.73, 2026-03-26), the same model implies only ~5.49% FCF CAGR -- comfortably inside the company's own guided and closely-tracked trajectory. The 16.5%-vs-5.5% gap is this run's own quantification of how much of the post-announcement re-rate (+136.5%) is deal-completion-odds/premium rather than a standalone re-rating; the reverse-DCF agent states explicitly it cannot separate the two without a disclosed offer price. Separately, the peer-relative method implies a much higher EUR79.2/share, but the valuation synthesis discounts this as mostly a peer-set composition effect (Uber/DoorDash/Prosus are larger, profitable, or holding-company businesses) and does not treat it as a clean market-implied read.
engine_view: The valuation module's own-financials-anchored triangulation (own-history EV/Sales reversion 45% weight, intrinsic DCF 15%, SOTP 18%, discounted peer-relative 22%) lands a base-case fair value of EUR39.65/share -- only 6.6% above the EUR37.20 price (thin margin of safety, 6.2%), bracketed by bull EUR49.01 and a 12-month operating bear of EUR18.59, with a separate multi-year structural/avoid-ruin floor of -EUR2.84/share if a regulatory shock and competitive erosion hit together. Read in isolation, the valuation module calls DHER 'Fairly valued (deal-contaminated)' -- not a standalone bargain, not obviously overpriced either. But the master synthesizer's probability-weighted scenario model -- blending deal-completion odds (self-constructed, since no module assigns them) with these standalone fair-value levels across 5 cases (bull 8%, base 52%, deal-breaks-standalone 22%, bear 12%, tail-structural 6%) -- computes a probability-weighted target price of EUR33.97, an expected return of -8.68%, a risk/reward of -0.17, and an 89.25% worst-case downside. The engine's real, decision-driving view is therefore not 'DHER standalone is mispriced' but 'the market's ~11.6% arb spread to an unverified ~EUR41.50 offer price is being treated as closer to a free arbitrage than the primary evidence supports,' once a hard auditor going-concern disqualifier (Glovo Spain, EUR440-770m contingent liability), GAAP-basis net leverage already past this run's own 6.0x stress-test ceiling (8.24x), 'Poor'-quality cash-light earnings (Critical-severity red flags), and a management change-of-control equity-vesting conflict are folded in. Final decision: Avoid.
what_everyone_knows: Uber announced an acquisition approach for Delivery Hero on 2026-07-16; Prosus/Naspers has irrevocably committed to tender its stake, pushing Uber's economic exposure over 50%; the deal is guided to close in H2 2027; the stock has risen from EUR15.73 (pre-announcement close, 2026-03-26) to EUR37.20 (+136.5%); sell-side Target Price and Recommendation consensus re-anchored to the deal within days of the announcement.
what_is_priced_in: A high probability of deal completion near a widely-circulated but web-sourced, primary-unconfirmed ~EUR41.50/share cash price, reflected in an ~11.6% arbitrage spread to the current price and a deal-contaminated Target Price consensus (mean EUR37.97). On the standalone operating side, the Street's Adjusted EBITDA/revenue/FCF estimate lines sit close to management's own guidance ('bar is fair') with quiet, non-debating revision activity -- but the reverse-DCF shows the all-in price itself embeds an aggressive ~16.5% FCF CAGR assumption, more than management's own operating guidance alone would justify, implying the gap between the fair operating bar and the aggressive DCF-implied growth is being filled by unpriced/underpriced deal-completion optimism plus credit for the FY2025 profitability inflection being durable.
what_market_may_be_missing: (1) The ~EUR41.50/share offer price that the whole 'clean 11.6% arbitrage' narrative rests on is unverified in every primary source reviewed -- no M&A call transcript, filing, or exchange notice in the data pool states a fixed per-share consideration; the 'spread' being traded is itself an assumption, not a fact. (2) Underneath that unverified spread sits a hard auditor going-concern note on Glovo Spain (KPMG, 'Material Uncertainty about the Ability of Subsidiaries to Continue as a Going Concern,' EUR440-770m contingent liability, unresolved because no FY2025 audited Annual Report exists yet); GAAP-basis net leverage (8.24x) already above this run's own illustrative 6.0x refinancing ceiling even though Adjusted-EBITDA-basis leverage (2.78x) looks moderate; 'Poor'-quality earnings (cash conversion collapsed to 8.8% in FY2025 from 92.2% in FY2024, with a ~EUR600-650m cash outflow excluded from the '+EUR250m FCF' headline via the same going-concern-linked exposure); and a management change-of-control provision that fully vests executives' equity on resignation -- a personal, price-independent incentive to see the deal close regardless of terms other shareholders get. Deal euphoria (target-price re-anchoring within days, quiet/non-debating operating-line revisions) appears to be discounting this risk cluster less than the primary evidence supports.
evidence_engine_is_different: Nothing conclusive. The engine's own final thesis states this explicitly: edge score 45/100, below its own 50-point proof bar for a claimed variant perception, and a subsequent adversarial pre-mortem review applied a further confidence haircut (confidence_score cut from 35 to 27; pre_mortem_verdict = 'Survives with haircut' -- the thesis direction was not falsified but conviction was reduced). The falsifiable test the engine itself set: if Uber's tender completes within the guided window at a confirmed price >= EUR41.50 with no minority squeeze-out dispute, and the FY2025 audited Annual Report shows the going-concern language resolved, this risk read was wrong. That test has not yet been run -- the evidence cited (unverified offer price, going-concern note, leverage-ceiling breach, cash-quality collapse, change-of-control conflict) is real and cited to primary/Tier-5 sources, but it is a risk-disclosure gap the market MAY be underweighting, not a demonstrated instance of the market actually mispricing it. No sell-side note, options-implied distribution, or short-interest data in this pool was checked against the risk cluster to show consensus is actually blind to it (no options/IBKR data exists in this pool at all per the final thesis's own positioning section).
base_rate_check: Respects the base rate on the standalone side: the reverse-DCF's aggressiveness call is anchored to DHER's own two-year decelerating growth trend, its own historical EV/Sales band (min 0.52x / mean 0.82x / median 0.73x / max 1.25x, no case exceeds this band), and its own disclosed cost of capital (10.7%-13.7%) rather than an externally borrowed comparator -- consistent with CLAUDE.md Section 9's same-metric/same-level/same-period discipline. The valuation module's own base case (EUR39.65) sits inside, not outside, DHER's own observed multiple range. However, the merger-arbitrage completion-probability judgment (bull 8% / base 52% / deal-breaks 22% / bear 12% / tail 6%) is a genuinely exceptional, self-constructed forecast -- no module in this run independently assigns deal-completion odds, and the scenario weights were built by the master synthesizer rather than derived from a governing base rate (e.g., historical completion rates for announced strategic-acquirer tender offers with an irrevocable anchor-shareholder commitment). That is flagged, not hidden, in the final thesis's own math section, but it means the -8.68% expected-return figure carries real, unquantified model risk on the probability side even though the underlying fair-value levels are conservatively grounded.
notes: Two different, non-interchangeable magnitudes exist in this run and neither by itself proves a robust edge: (1) the valuation module's own standalone base fair value (EUR39.65) is only +6.6% above price (EUR37.20) -- essentially 'fairly valued,' a thin gap sitting inside the noise created by a +215% own-history-vs-peer method disagreement and a deal-contaminated price; (2) the master synthesizer's probability-weighted target (EUR33.97, built from self-constructed deal-completion odds) implies -8.68% expected return -- the more decision-relevant number since it is what the Avoid rating and this report's gap_direction/gap_magnitude_pct are keyed to, but it depends heavily on an unvalidated probability distribution over a binary M&A outcome, not on an independently corroborated base rate. Edge score is kept low because: the engine's own edge score (45/100) sits below its own stated 50-point proof bar; the pre-mortem review already cut confidence from 35 to 27; the entire bull+base probability mass (60%) and the negative expected return both hinge on the same single unverified assumption (the ~EUR41.50 offer price); and no independent evidence (options-implied distribution, short interest, a second corroborating source on the risk cluster being underpriced) exists in the pool to show the market is actually blind to the flagged risks rather than already partially discounting them via the Hold rating and 2.86 average recommendation. This is a real, well-cited caution flag, not yet a provable mispricing -- consistent with the run's own 'Avoid' (a risk-driven rejection, not a variant-perception-driven short) rather than a high-conviction directional call.
